course_name_original: General and academic Dutch - intermediate level
course_name_en: General and academic Dutch - intermediate level
prerequisites: Lower B1 level of the CEFR

learning_outcomes.text: Understand (reading or listening): the argumentative scheme of factual texts, television programmes and newspapers written in current language and related to cultural matters or contemporary problems; academic course notes related to his field of study; most of an academic lecture related to his field of study; a normal conversation. Level: B1+

Speak: expose his points of view and defend them; keep, with some ease, a conversation or discussion with a native speaker, in standard language, on a general topic or a topic related to his field of study. Level B1+
Write: a simple and coherent text on a familiar topic which is of direct interest to him or which is related to his field of study. Level B1-
The student has a knowledge of Dutch and Flemish cultural aspects and is able to use the appropriate strategies to establish contacts with native speakers.
The student can perceive the differences and similitudes between his own culture and the culture of the target language.

syllabus_topics: Individual presentations of a previously selected press article
Group presentations on a topic related to the Flemish culture
Group presentations on a topic related to the students' field of study
A cultural trip to Flanders (visit of a Flemish town or an exhibition) chosen, prepared and organized by the students (or PowerPoint presentation if conditions don't allow)
teaching_methods: Distance learning mode (using Teams and Moodle)
Self-tuition syllabus for general and academic vocabulary, and specific grammatical structures with exercises and keys
Oral practice activities for vocabulary and grammar revision
Self-tuition tests on Moodle e-learning Platform
Preparation for debates, discussions, and presentations

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment (class participation, daily work, individual presentation of a press article)
Oral test at the end of the quadrimester (group presentation on a topic selected by the students)
Oral interactive exam in group of 2 or 3 students at the end of the term or in January based on the different topics and role-plays seen during the lessons

assessment_rules: The 'absorbent absence' system applies: all parts of the tests are compulsory, and absence (without official proof) for one part implies an 'absence' mark for the entire evaluation. Students failing the January test or not providing a medical certificate must retake the exam in the August session. Attendance is compulsory, and the teacher may suggest the jury oppose registration for the exam if a student has not regularly followed activities. In the August session, students must complete an assignment and an oral exam; permanent assessment marks are considered only if beneficial to the student.
